utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. May I remind you, sir, that the affirmation that you made to tell the truth still applies. Yes, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mazreku, regarding the events from 1998, you said that the police had brought you to a lawn in front of the school and that some of the young men had been taken into the school building where they had been abused and questioned, beaten up. So are you able to describe for us what actually happened on that occasion, and why were those young men taken inside the school building? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness doesn't seem to hear anything.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where is the Albanian interpreter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sorry, you may have to repeat that question, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, now I hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mazreku. My question takes us back to 1998 when you explained to us all that the police had brought you to a lawn in front of the school building. You said that some young men had been taken inside the building and that some of them had been beaten up or whatever it was that happened to them. Do you know what actually happened inside the school building and why those young men were taken in?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were young people. They were taken to the school, and they were beaten up, and then later they were imprisoned. They were taken to Prizren. Some of them did a prison term.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me how many young men were taken inside the school building and how many had been taken to Prizren, do you know that, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the accurate number, but I would say three or four were taken from there. They were told that they were KLA members.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mazreku, if you can answer my question now, did anything happen to any of those young men after they were taken? You said that some of them served the prison sentences, others were released, or what is it that actually happened to all the others?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't with them, and I don't know what happened to them. But they themselves said that they took us to this place. They -- some of them were taken to Leskovc, some to Nis, I don't know. But I only know they did this prison term.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did all of them survive?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they are alive. They did the prison sentence, and they returned home.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mazreku, let me move on to 1999 now. In your statement of the 15th of January, 2000 - at page 3, paragraph 5 in B/C/S; page 3, paragraph 8 in English, and page 3, paragraph 7 in the Albanian - you say: "I saw a total of seven to eight tanks. I saw that around the 20" -- or "I saw 20, 30, or maybe even 40 Serbs. They were wearing black military uniforms and on their backs and on their sleeves it said 'police' in Cyrillic." So my first question is this: Those tank, where did you see those seven or eight tanks?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me about 1999 or 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: All my questions now pertain to 1999, Mr. Mazreku, and to the massacre that you described where 106 of your fellow citizens were killed.

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will tell you. There were seven or eight tanks that I already mentioned in my statement, and they were in a place higher than the village. And they were not wearing black clothes but they were wearing military clothes, and on their back it was written "milicija."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: But tell me, were those military tanks the tanks that belonged to the Yugoslav Army? What colour were they?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were tanks of the army, and they had the SMB colour. You know what the SMB is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I know. Mr. Mazreku, tell me, you said that they had military uniforms, olive drab uniforms, but were they camouflage uniforms? I'm talking about the green uniforms now.

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were of like grass green colour. The normal colour that the Serb military had.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mazreku, yesterday when my learned colleague showed you the insignia, you indicated some patches but I don't know whether you saw when you were shown the insignia, the insignia where it said police in Cyrillic, but you didn't point them out.

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already indicated it. I put a circle there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you whether you saw the insignia where it said "police" when my learned friend showed you. It didn't say "police" on the insignia that you have circled. So I'm just asking you whether you saw them or not as you were looking at the photo file with the insignia of the army and the police?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I think I circled it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Perhaps the time-frame for the insignias that were shown to the witness could be clarified. My understanding was the Defence counsel was asking him questions in relation to 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He is at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And I'm not sure if it's appropriate for me to provide this information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, I don't think it is. Thank you, Ms. Gopalan. Carry on, please, Mr. Djordjevic. Bear in mind, there may be a significant difference between insignia and a full marking across the back of a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Interpretation yes, definitely, Your Honour. Let me just consult my assistant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Can we please have on our screens the spread or the photo file with insignia. That's P00327 from the 65 ter list. Let's start with the page 1. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mazreku, could you please look at those insignia here. You said that it said police on their backs, and you said that on their sleeves and on their uniforms they also had similar patches. Do you see on the screen in front of you any such patches, and if yes, could you please indicate what number it is marked with?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And could you tell me some of the patches that you see here, were they worn on the sleeves?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were with the Serbian flag, and the four Ss.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: What is the number, Mr. Mazreku?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Serbian flag, this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Number 3?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't see the four Ss here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Is any of them --

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender this page by page, or in fact perhaps we could go to the next page and then I could tender it as a whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This is already an exhibit. Exhibit P327, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do know that, but I don't think that it's been marked in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This one hasn't been marked. He has said that he saw some 6 and number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and that's why I would like this page to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's already in evidence and the witness says that on this exhibit he recognizes number 6 and number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move on to the next page. If you could perhaps zoom in a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mazreku, you looked at this spread yesterday and I believe that you marked the patch number 9 and patch number 13. Now I would like you to look very carefully now, we are talking about 1999 and the forces that entered the village on that day, the 31st of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1999 there was this patch with the Serbian flag, as a symbol, those that -- that that belonged to the police who massacred us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: But could you tell me which is the insignia? What number?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I showed the one in the previous picture, that belonged to the Serbian police. Milosevic party that was in power. These patches were before in the past when there were four, five parties in 1988. I haven't seen any of these that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: So we can agree that none of these patches was worn by the army of killers, as you called them, on that day; is that so, Mr. Mazreku? None of these markings that you are looking at now?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. There was only one patch, the one that was worn by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: But you can't see it here on this photograph, is that so?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see here the Yugoslav or the Serbian flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have the next page. No. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: So let us conclude then that the patch worn by the troops, by the military, the police there, that they wore a Yugoslav flag, that they had the Yugoslav flag on the patch; am I right when I say that?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police were wearing that sign that I showed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the previous photograph, we will agree. But I'm asking you whether the coat of arms, the emblem contained the Yugoslav flags, that's what I want you to confirm. And you said that it also had the four Ss on it, if I'm not mistaken?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were also four letter S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, my next question will follow up on this effort to identify those units. You said that they wore, in the statement that I quoted, black uniforms, black military uniforms. Could you please explain to me since you said today that they had green uniforms, the black military uniforms, were they in fact dark green? Were they darker and that's why you called them black or is it something else? Because you repeat that in your statement, the statement that you gave on the 21st of May, 2008, you know, so I don't want that to cause any confusion for the Trial Chamber and everybody else in this trial, so I would like you to explain this.

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I already indicated that in 1999 they were wearing green. Dark green, olive green colour, and on their backs it was written milicija. There was no other colour. The colour wasn't black, but it was the green colour of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I understand perfectly what you are saying now. I just wish to ask you to tell me why is it stated in your statement that the uniforms were black? Just explain that, please.

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned black in reference to 1998, not to 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: That is it, I'm asking you this precisely because it emanates from the context in your statement that the uniforms were black. That is why I asked you this question.

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying no. It wasn't black, it was green.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I shall not dwell on this question any more. Please tell me what were these soldiers, policemen, killers, as you call them, wearing on their heads, if anything?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I don't remember. Plus we were so upset at that moment that we couldn't watch around us. I don't know whether they had hats or not. They started to shoot at us with automatic rifles, and they killed us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mazreku, did you do military service in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: When did you finish your service?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went in 1960 and finished in 1962. I was in the army for two years.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Which combat arm were you in?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the infantry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: You say that they fired from automatic rifles. Can you tell me what weapons they had, they were carrying? Could you identify the weapons?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Automatic weapons. In Serbian they were called "automata." They were short weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Were these the so-called Kalashnikovs or another type of automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know their name. They were automatic weapons, and they had magazines, and they loaded the weapons right in front of our eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, apart from tanks, did you see any other vehicles and which?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen other vehicles other than the tank. I'm talking about that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: It is only that day that we are talking about right now.

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day there weren't any other vehicles other than the tanks, and they were heavy-calibre tanks. "Samohotka" is what they're called.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: And these vehicles, were they also of olive-drab colour?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: And in addition to these soldiers in dark green uniforms of a single colour as you described them, were there any other troops present there or in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were in the tanks, but the first time there were 30 to 40 policemen who surrounded us. I have not seen any other police or military forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You refer to persons called Tahir Krasniqi, and Haxhi Krasniqi, I believe. These persons who gave around 4.000 marks, I'm not going to speculate on the exact sum, to two Serbs in order to try to propitiate them in that way. Tell me, this Haxhi Krasniqi, is his name Hadji or Hadjiu, Haxhi, what is his name?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact his real name was Emin. Then he went for --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Is his surname Haxhil?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why we started to call him Haxhi. So he went to Mecca and became Haxhi. But his original name was Emin Krasniqi and then he became Haxhi Emin Krasniqi. But in the statement I've said Haxhi because that's how he was known to all of us. He gave the money to them. They said they want more and then all of us collected whatever we had, but that wasn't enough for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, did you see any of those policemen carrying in some kind of bags any valuables that they had taken from women?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them as they were taking stuff from children and women, they took all the golden stuff and they took it to the -- in two bags, and they took it to the people in the tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: How far was this tank from where you were?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 3-, to 400 metres from where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, the women and the children, they were sent off in the direction of Albania. In the end, did they stay in Kosovo or did they indeed leave and go to Albania?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, they couldn't go into Albania, cross into Albania, because they were not allowed. And all of us, the rest of us, we remained in the village of Ciflak until the war ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The supplement which we received you corrected yourself and you said that you were actually referring to the Roma, i.e., gypsies, when you observed people of a dark complexion. What I should like to know is whether all these soldiers, i.e., policemen, had paint on their faces or just some of them?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Couldn't absolutely observe what their faces were like. I could not tell whether they had tanned faces or painted faces, but some of them looked darker than others.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did any of your fellow townsmen, and I'm referring to both men and women, recognise a single man? And you yourself said that you didn't, that's why I'm not asking you that question.

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were not able to recognise any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mazreku, were you present at the burials of the victims on the 2nd of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there and only seven to eight or ten maximum were buried. Then I went to stay with my son, my children, because I was injured and I needed attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, where were the remaining 99 people buried?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all buried there. 106 were buried there. Each of them has a grave there and their name and there is a commemorative plaque with the names on, those who were buried there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know who Hamid Krasniqi is?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hamid Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no Hamid Krasniqi in our village. There was one but he died.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: This Hamid Krasniqi that you just referred to, is he perhaps from Drenovik, or Drenovac, I'm not sure what this neighbouring village is called?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him. I'm talking about what I know and what I've said. This one I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because some of the previous witnesses who talked about this subject said that he attended the funeral, that he was in civilian clothes, but that they knew that he was a KLA member and that is why I'm asking you this question, have I managed to jog your memory? Do you now recall who this is?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this man is the one who is, then he is from Drenoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: So did he attend the funeral?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him, because I told you that in the evening we buried about eight to ten bodies, and that's approximate, and the following morning I went to my children because I was injured. I don't know whether he took part or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what had you heard about him, about this one from Drenovac?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: You just said awhile ago that is the one from Drenovik, that means that you know him, that is why I'm asking you what do you know?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe he has been, maybe the one from Drenoc has been there, but I didn't see him. There is one Hamid Krasniqi from Drenoc, but I didn't see him. And if don't see something, I cannot say something about it. I'm here to tell the truth and whatever I know, I will say. If I don't know, don't push me, because I can't say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I understood that you hadn't seen him, but as I can see that you know who this is. Do you know that he was a member of the KLA? That is what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did I know? I was not interested in what he was. I know that all the Albanian population in their hearts were KLA, but we did not have weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, where was this KLA after which all the Albanian population -- around which all the Albanian population rallied?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in the mountains, where else could they be? They did not have barracks like a proper army, so they were out there in the mountains.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in which mountains were they that you know about?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what mountains. I was not entitled, and I didn't have the knowledge, and I was not responsible to know where, what mountains they were in, and so on. I only was responsible for my own family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there was fighting between the Serbian forces and the KLA in the area of your municipality, and if you do know, what is it that you know?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no fighting between the KLA and the Serbian forces in our village, in my area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Were there any KLA members from your village?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Sahit Mazreku, and his son Salhi?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sahit Mazreku is a cousin, and he was also injured, he was part of my group, part of the group that I was in. And he died after the war. He escaped the massacre, he survived the massacre. He lived for another four years, then he died. I also know his son Salhi. They are cousins of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that your relative Salhi was a member of the KLA and that he transported the KLA members from village to village?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that he was a KLA member. He was a teacher. He was teaching kids. He wasn't a KLA member.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were hurt. Were you wounded in the back? Were you operated on?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the war I was operated on because at the time there was no -- there were no facilities to do that, there was no treatment, so I had to suffer with my wounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mazreku, thank you, I have no further questions for you. Your Honour, this completes my cross-examination of Mr. Mazreku.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djordjevic. Ms. Gopalan, do you have re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mazreku.

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I have a few questions for you this morning.

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And this is in relation to some of the questions that were put to you by Defence counsel. I'd like to take you back to what you said about the people you were with in the Kosnik mountains, if you remember. You said that there were at least 2.000 to 3.000 people and that they had come from various municipalities. And if you remember, you said that there were far too many people there. This is at page 61, 83.

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, in relation to these people who you were with in the mountains, do you know why they were there in the mountains?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were there because they feared for their lives because when they started burning the people's houses, then they ran away to save their lives. They were scared of being massacred because there were people in Drenoc who were massacred. That was the reason why they were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, when you say they feared for their lives because of the burnings of the houses, could you tell us how it is you learned that these people feared for their lives?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everyone was scared because from everywhere there was firing, shelling, there were weapons being fired, and houses burning and everyone was scared. They were running for their lives. The children were traumatized because of the firing and we were -- we were begging them not to fire their weapons because the children were terrified.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, who is it you were begging not to fire the weapons at you?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: We asked the militia not to shoot in the air because our children were being scared to death.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The policemen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about 1998 when they surrounded us in the Kosnik mountain.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also mentioned the people being massacred in Drenoc. How did you learn about this massacre?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Qen Gashi and there was also a woman, I do not know her. There was Jakup Krasniqi, Mereme Morina, and another woman, I did not know her name. There were some four or five people who were massacred during the offensive, the night before. They were found in their houses. They were old people, they were elderly people who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Who told you about these killings, Mr. Mazreku?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: We only heard about the detail of who was killed when we came back to our house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And who told you these details?

utterances.speaker: AVDYL MAZREKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the villagers. The young men in the village. They were telling us about what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mazreku. I have no further questions for you this morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are welcome, and thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mazreku, you'll be pleased to know that that concludes the questions for you. The Chamber wishes to thank you for coming to The Hague and for the assistance that you've been able to give to us in what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I wish you every success in your work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. You may now, of course, return to your normal activities, and the court officer will assist you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, Defence counsel, we regret to inform you that we do not have another witness available for today. The next witness, Mr. Haxhiu, will be available tomorrow morning. We are trying to get one of the crime based witnesses from next week moved to this week, but we will only be able to provide further information on that witness later on today. But for the moment, there is no witness available for the remainder of our court sitting today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is the movement of Mr. Hax hiu.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhiu arrived late last night, and he is being proofed from early this morning. And we think he will be available -- he will be available to testify tomorrow morning at the earliest, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may. I'm afraid Mr. Haxhiu is only available tomorrow -- on Thursday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Very shortly and briefly. [Interpretation] When we made arrangements as to how we would proceed here in the courtroom in this trial before your Chamber, we agreed that we would always strive to be ready for the next witness, in situations such as this one. But of course it requires that we be notified promptly about any problems that the Prosecution encounters, and, I believe, their objective in nature. At this point in time, I don't have any documents or anything. I don't even know the name of our potential next witness. The documents are in my office and in order to be able to do anything, I would have to go back to my office to learn the identity of the witness and to see whether I would take this witness or my colleague, Mr. Djurdjic. As you know, our team is small, and we are really doing our best to make sure that this trial proceeds efficiently. As lead counsel, I'm really trying to make sure that it does and to organise myself as well as I can. And I really regret the fact that my colleagues did not inform us by e-mail last night that the witness had only arrived yesterday, and that they are not ready to take him. So I am afraid that we can't really proceed today. I cannot agree to defend my client in an irregular situation, and I cannot get organised to do that within the next hour, two hours, or three hours. That is all I have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be apparent, I'm sure, to counsel that this is not a satisfactory position in the view of the Chamber. The limited number of witnesses who were on the list for this week, last week, and next week has already been the subject of comment. The week of the 29th list also has a small number of witnesses, that has come out since we commented. It is clear that there remain some witnesses whose evidence will be relatively brief. So efforts will need to be made to correct the position so that we do not lose time simply because a witness is not ready to proceed. A comment you made, Ms. Gopalan, leaves me a little unclear. Were you intending to say that the next witness cannot be available until tomorrow or were you meaning to say the witness cannot be available after tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next witness arrives tonight and he will be available tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that the witness that you earlier said was here and being proofed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That was a mistake on my part, Your Honours. He is arriving today so he has not been proofed yet. But he is the witness that we indicated in our notification. The change in the situation is simply that he is not available today but will only be available tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: One witness from last week has not been called. Is that a continuing problem?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I will have to check that, Your Honours. Perhaps you could clarify for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Hoxha.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Hani Hoxha?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Just a moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, Hani Hoxha has already testified and he testified on the 5th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that clears that one up. The notification that you made on the 2nd of June indicated that the next witness and the last witness for this week would be Mr. Haxhiu. I mention that because it would seem that there should be no difficulty in the Defence being ready to deal with Mr. Haxhiu when he is called because he has been on the list since the notification of the 2nd of June. Let us hope that you are able to find an additional witness so that we do not lose time on Friday as well as today. It seems we can do nothing now but adjourn to continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask something. It isn't clear for tomorrow, is it the witness Baton Haxhiu or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is that witness. There may be a witness from next week brought forward for Friday of this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: For Friday, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Tomorrow it is Haxhiu.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, short remark. [Interpretation] I would like to ask my learned friend or rather the Prosecution if possible to indicate who the possible witness for Friday is. That's all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As I understand it, that is premature. Attempts are being made to bring a witness forward. But as soon as that is known, there should be an immediate notification both to Mr. Djordjevic and to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. We will certainly provide that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, you've carried off the role of being in the hot seat very charmingly. We will adjourn and continue tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 18th day of June, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.12 a.m.,
